claim.pdf_says: Figure E.5 — Hierarchy of queues: a tree with levels QUEUE (A), SUB-QUEUE (1) (B, C), SUB-QUEUE (2) (D, E under B; F, G under C), SUB-QUEUE (3) (H, I under D; J, K under E; L, M under F; N, O under G) and MESSAGE (H: Z1 X2; I: X3 X4 X5; J: X1 Y3 Y5 Z5; K: Z6 Z7 Y6; L: Y7 Y8; M: Y1 Y2; N: X6; O: Z2 Z3 Z4 Y4).
claim.why_it_matters: The tree structure is lost: the SUB-QUEUE (3) level label and sub-queue-3 names H, J, K, L, M and N are missing, the parent/child edges are gone, and 'MESSAGE' displaced X2's column so the message lists no longer line up under their sub-queues. The worked examples on page 762 (e.g. Sub-queue-3 N returns Message X6; Queue A returns Z1) cannot be followed from the markdown. Annex E is informative, so no normative rule is lost.

verdict.reasoning: Printed page 739 (PDF p761) shows Figure E.5 as a tree: QUEUE A; SUB-QUEUE (1) B, C; SUB-QUEUE (2) D, E under B and F, G under C; SUB-QUEUE (3) H, I under D, J, K under E, L, M under F, N, O under G; message lists Z1 X2 / X3 X4 X5 / X1 Y3 Y5 Z5 / Z6 Z7 Y6 / Y7 Y8 / Y1 Y2 / X6 / Z2 Z3 Z4 Y4. The markdown keeps only I and O of the sub-queue-3 names, omits the SUB-QUEUE (3) level label and all edges, and places 'MESSAGE' in the first column of the third message row, so the hierarchy needed to follow the page-762 worked examples cannot be recovered. The claim quotes both sources accurately. The content loss is genuine but sits in informative Annex E.
